executiveSummary: Multiple high-impact, OT-relevant advisories and actively exploited vulnerabilities are in play this week. Adversaries continue to target edge infrastructure, remote access, and industrial control protocols to establish footholds and enable potential disruption. Priority action is required on internet-exposed routers/switches, ICS protocol endpoints (OPC UA, CC-Link IE TSN, S7comm), and grid, water/wastewater, and transportation support systems. Active nation-state and hacktivist activity against OT/ICS: pro-Russia groups opportunistically brute-force exposed VNC to HMIs/SCADA causing loss of view and parameter tampering; separate U.S. advisories warn of Iranian-affiliated actors modifying PLC logic and of AI-assisted reconnaissance against Siemens S7 PLCs. CISA Advisory CISA Advisory CISA Advisory Grid stability risk: Hitachi Energy FACTS Control Platform (FCP) GWS component has multiple critical flaws enabling unauthorized parameter changes; patching and strict isolation are required. CISA ICS Advisory Industrial protocol exposures: CC-Link IE TSN weakness (no vendor fix) can allow I/O tampering/DoS on the same segment; Eclipse Milo OPC UA server vulnerabilities allow auth bypass, info disclosure, and DoS-patch and harden immediately. CISA ICS Advisory CISA Bulletin Edge device exploitation continues: MikroTik RouterOS exploit chain is being used in the wild; Zyxel GS1900 switches are in CISA KEV for active exploitation; Cisco Secure Email Gateway SQLi is actively exploited. CERT Polska CISA KEV CISA KEV Energy/transport OT-adjacent: EV charging, ActiveMQ brokers, Danfoss iC7 drives, rail diagnostics FDS 102, and FreeRTOS/Mongoose library issues feature in recent CISA bulletins; segment networks, patch fast, and apply compensating controls. CISA Bulletin CISA Bulletin

relevance: Why this matters now Multiple advisories describe active, repeatable intrusion paths that cross the IT/OT boundary: exposed VNC, compromised routers/switches, vulnerable email gateways, and analytics platforms. Industrial protocol exposure (OPC UA, CC-Link IE TSN, S7comm) elevates the blast radius if adversaries gain a foothold-enabling loss of view/control or unauthorized parameter changes. Grid, water/wastewater, and transport EVSE dependencies are directly affected by current vulnerability sets. Most at-risk environments Operators with internet-exposed HMIs/SCADA remote access (VNC/RDP/VPN) or weak MFA/allowlists. Enterprises relying on MikroTik/Zyxel/Cisco edge devices with delayed patching or default management exposure. Sites using Eclipse Milo OPC UA servers, Hitachi Energy FACTS FCP, Danfoss iC7 drives, or CC-Link IE TSN on flat L2 segments.

descriptions: Initial Access: Exploitation of public-facing apps (Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-8452 PoC; Zimbra CVE-2025-66376) and edge/KEV devices (Zyxel/MikroTik/Cisco SEG). Supporting Report CISA KEV
Lateral Movement: Abuse of VNC/RDP/WinRM; rdp2tcp; Impacket atexec; VPN portals; identity abuse in Entra ID/OAuth (CISA red team lessons). CISA Advisory
Command & Control: MQTT/Matrix (Toy Ghouls); covert SOHO/IoT proxies (China-nexus); reverse tunnels; Azure/Cloudflare fronting (Mirage Kitten). Kaspersky CISA Advisory
Impact: Loss of view and parameter manipulation (VNC HMIs); potential grid instability (FACTS); PLC logic alteration (Iranian-affiliated APT). CISA Advisory ICS Advisory

outlook72h: Expect continued scanning/exploitation attempts for Zyxel GS1900 and MikroTik RouterOS; validate remediation and monitor for persistence. Watch for opportunistic VNC brute forcing against HMIs/SCADA; preempt with exposure reviews and lockouts. Accelerate OPC UA server and FACTS FCP patch windows; implement compensating controls where immediate patching is not possible. Monitor Zimbra/NetScaler perimeters for post-PoC copycat exploitation; tighten WAF and log review.
